programs.name: a2b
programs.purpose: Convert ASCII floating-point values to native binary floats.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: A2B - convert ascii floats to binary

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of floats per vector; input whitespace need not follow line boundaries.

params.name: outpar
params.description: Output parameter file receiving n2, the number of complete vectors.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Conversion uses the platform's fscanf float parsing and native float representation. An incomplete final vector causes an error.
programs.difficulty_reason: It parses and writes fixed-size vectors of floats.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | b2a n1=2 format=0 outpar=/dev/null | a2b n1=2 outpar=/dev/null > out.bin

test_cases.description: Parse four-float vectors in decimal notation.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | b2a n1=4 format=1 outpar=/dev/null | a2b n1=4 outpar=/dev/null > out.bin

programs.name: a2i
programs.purpose: Convert lines of ASCII numeric values to native binary integers.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: A2I - convert Ascii to binary Integers

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of values read from each input line.

params.name: outpar
params.description: Output parameter file receiving n, the number of input lines.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Each value is parsed as float and rounded with NINT before conversion to int; out-of-range conversions can have undefined behavior. Input is processed in fixed-size line buffers.
programs.difficulty_reason: It parses each input line and rounds its values to integers.

test_cases.description: Convert two values per line to integers.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | b2a n1=2 format=0 outpar=/dev/null | a2i n1=2 outpar=/dev/null > out.int

test_cases.description: Convert scaled values with four values per line.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | farith op=scale scale=2.5 | b2a n1=4 format=1 outpar=/dev/null | a2i n1=4 outpar=/dev/null > out.int

programs.name: b2a
programs.purpose: Convert native binary floats to formatted ASCII lines.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: B2A - convert binary floats to ascii

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of floats per output line.

params.name: format
params.description: Zero prints scientific notation; any nonzero value prints fixed-point notation with 20 digits after the decimal.

params.name: outpar
params.description: Output parameter file receiving n, the number of output lines.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Formatting uses the platform's printf and locale. The code's nonzero format is %20.20f, although the selfdoc describes %15.15f.
programs.difficulty_reason: It reads fixed-size groups of floats and formats them as text.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | b2a n1=2 format=0 outpar=/dev/null > out.txt

test_cases.description: Print fixed-point notation in groups of four.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | b2a n1=4 format=1 outpar=/dev/null > out.txt

programs.name: farith
programs.purpose: Apply arithmetic operations to native binary float files or streams.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: FARITH - File ARITHmetic -- perform simple arithmetic with binary files

params.name: in
params.description: First input filename; omitted means standard input.

params.name: out
params.description: Output filename; omitted means standard output.

params.name: in2
params.description: Second input filename or scalar; required for add, sub, mul, div, cartprod, slowp and slothp. The latter three branches nevertheless read a file pointer even when a scalar was parsed.

params.name: n
params.description: Number of first-input floats for cartprod; required when op=cartprod.

params.name: isig
params.description: First zero-based index whose sign is flipped; required when op=signum.

params.name: op
params.description: Operation: noop, neg, abs, scale, bias, exp, sin, cos, log, sqrt, sqr, degrad, raddeg, pinv, pinvsqr, pinvsqrt, add, sub, mul, div, cartprod, signum, sloth, slowp, or slothp.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Math-library transcendental functions operate in double and are assigned to float; other expressions mix float and double constants. sloth computes (1.0/x)*x and slothp computes (1/x)*x - (1/x2)*x2, rather than the documented reciprocal squares. Scalar in2 with cartprod, slowp or slothp leaves in2fp null and leads to invalid file access.
programs.difficulty_reason: It has many unary and binary operations and buffers the first input for Cartesian products.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | farith op=scale scale=2.5 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Add a scalar to each sample.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | farith op=add in2=1.25 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Multiply two binary files sample by sample.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip > in2.bin && suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | farith op=mul in2=in2.bin > out.bin

test_cases.description: Form a Cartesian product of two small input vectors.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=4 ntr=1 | sustrip > in2.bin && suplane nt=4 ntr=1 | sustrip | farith op=cartprod n=4 in2=in2.bin > out.bin

programs.name: float2ibm
programs.purpose: Convert native binary floats to IBM-format floating-point words.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: FLOAT2IBM - convert native binary FLOATS to IBM tape FLOATS

params.name: endian
params.default: computed: detected host byte order, 1 for big endian and 0 for little endian
params.description: Selects byte swapping in the usual conversion implementation.

params.name: outpar
params.description: Output parameter file receiving n, the number of converted values.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The conversion assumes 32-bit IEEE floats and 32-bit int, loses up to three mantissa bits, and does not specially handle IEEE subnormals, infinities, NaNs or negative zero. It aliases float storage through int pointers and uses signed shifts that can be undefined or implementation-dependent. The HPUX branch ignores endian.
programs.difficulty_reason: It converts each float independently with integer masks and shifts.

test_cases.description: Convert samples using detected byte order.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | float2ibm outpar=/dev/null > out.ibm

test_cases.description: Convert samples with explicit little-endian selection.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | float2ibm endian=0 outpar=/dev/null > out.ibm
suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | float2ibm endian=1 outpar=/dev/null > out.ibm

programs.name: ftnstrip
programs.purpose: Remove Fortran record-length delimiters from binary records.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: FTNSTRIP - convert a file of binary data plus record delimiters created
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Record markers are interpreted as native int byte counts; the trailer is read but not checked against the header. Malformed or truncated records are not reliably validated.
programs.difficulty_reason: It copies each record payload after reading its length and discards the trailer.

test_cases.command: suspike nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | ftnunstrip n1=1 outpar=/dev/null | ftnstrip > out.bin
suplane nt=16 ntr=2 | sustrip | ftnunstrip n1=8 outpar=/dev/null | ftnstrip > out.bin
